text: I'll start by exploring the workspace.
The root cause is visible: line 18 forcibly ASCII-encodes the input and drops every non-ASCII character. Let me confirm with the test run.
The test reproduces the issue: "José Martínez" becomes "Jos Martnez".

args.root_cause: In `parse_orders_csv`, the first line of the function is `text = text.encode("ascii", errors="ignore").decode("ascii")`. This forcibly re-encodes the entire CSV text to ASCII, silently dropping every non-ASCII character before the CSV is parsed. Any accented letter in customer_name (e.g. "é", "í", "Å") is removed, producing "Jos Martnez". Only rows with non-ASCII names are affected, matching the report. The ASCII-only filter is unnecessary for csv.DictReader, which handles Unicode text correctly, so the line should be removed (or the input decoded properly from bytes with the correct encoding, e.g. UTF-8, at the file-read boundary).
